title: The Future of Banking: Strategy for the AI Era
underlying_data_time: Bank assets at 2025 year-end; return analysis 2025
figure_ref: Figure 2 — Banks with leadership positions have measurably better returns
business_context: Bain compares return on equity across business areas in major global banks classified by market leadership. Leading positions are associated with 15% ROE versus 9% for weaker positions. The exhibit is an association, not an experiment identifying a causal effect.
key_message: Business-area market leadership correlates with higher ROE: 15% versus 9% among the surveyed top 30 banks.
so_what: Prioritize defending or building defensible leadership where economics justify it; do not assume the 6pp ROE association is causal.
original_chart_type: Two-category vertical bar, weak gray and leading red
encoding: x=leadership group; y=ROE%; bar fill=leadership class; direct labels; zero axis

data_spec.period: Bank assets at 2025 year-end; return analysis 2025

data_recipe: Select a consistent population of large banks and define business-area leadership using disclosed ranks.
Assign each comparable business area to weak or leading based on rank thresholds.
Compute ROE with the same measurement date, weighting policy and profitability definition.
Plot both values against a shared zero baseline, with exact direct labels.
Test composition, survivorship and endogeneity before claiming causal effects.
message_conditions: Top 30 publicly traded banks ranked by 2025 assets; the sample is not all banks.
Weak and leading refer to market-position classes across 18 business areas.
Reported returns are averages/benchmark comparisons; underlying bank-level estimates and weighting were not disclosed.
design_moves: Kind comparison_bar; color/layout/context configurable via THEME and CONTEXT
Direct labels and careful unit/denominator distinction
All positions computed from data and series order
diff_notes: Opened actual Flourish Figure 2 thumbnail; shape, ordering, colors, labels and two reported values reproduced. Font and vertical whitespace are not pixel-identical.
